title: Modules
explain: A module is just a `.py` file you can import from another file. `import math` gives you its tools under the `math.` prefix, while `from math import sqrt` brings in one name directly. The standard library has hundreds of modules ready to use.
code:
import math
from random import choice
from datetime import date

print(math.sqrt(16))                 # 4.0
print(math.pi)
print(choice(["rock", "paper", "scissors"]))
print(date.today().year >= 2024)     # True
exercise: Use `random.randint` to roll two dice and print their sum.
tip: Never name your own file the same as a module you import, like `random.py`, or Python will import your file instead.
